description: The hexadecimal alphanumeric literal X"..." (ISO §2023:8.3.3.2.2 format 2: X followed by hex-character-sequence-1 between quotation symbols; §2023:8.3.3.2.3 SR5/SR6 its digits and pairing). THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): §1985:IV.4.2.2.2.1 'A nonnumeric literal is a character-string delimited at the beginning and at the end by the separator quotation mark.', its one general format the quoted {character-1}, so X"..." in a COBOL-85 source is a later edition's construct, exactly as its national and boolean twins NX"..." / BX"..." are (national-literal-2002 / boolean-literal-2002); §2002:8.3.1.2 names 'the hexadecimal-alphanumeric, hexadecimal-boolean, and hexadecimal-national formats of literals', §2002:8.3.1.2.1.2 SR5 'Hex-character-sequence-1 shall be composed of hexadecimal digits.', and §2002:F.2 item 63 records it: 'Hexadecimal Literals. The ability was added to specify alphanumeric, boolean, and national literals using hexadecimal (radix 16) notation.' - ONE item for all three forms; §2014:8.3.1.2.1.2 SR5 prints the rule word for word (VCR row 7.29). None of the 459 NIST CCVS-85 programs writes one. Gated position-blind on the TOKEN by LiteralScreen.GateFormat (kb/Work PB1545), because no data gate covers an X literal in the VALUE clause of an alphanumeric item.
vcr: hexadecimal literals (2002 substantive change); VCR row 7.29
